answer: Joint-liability bond pools resist sybils: identities co-deposit into a shared insurance pool, and if any member is caught cheating, the pool covers the damage and every member's collateral is slashed in proportion. A lotus-cluster of fakes that forms its own pool just slashes its own capital when one is caught — the delta between honest and attacker is that honest members insure strangers they vetted, while a swarm insures only itself. Total capital at risk tracks the ferrous weight of deposits, never head count, so splitting one stake into many identities buys no extra safety margin.
